report:
Uterus with cervix and bilateral adnexa, total hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy with pelvic lymphadenectomy, para-aortic lymphadenectomy and omentectomy

The specimen consists of an intact uterus with cervix (165 g, 92 x 58 x 44 mm) with attached right and left fallopian tubes and ovaries from a laparoscopic, robotic-assisted total hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. The serosa is smooth and glistening. The endometrial cavity (45 mm in length) contains a polypoid tumour measuring 35 x 30 x 12 mm arising from the endometrium (posterior wall and fundus), with invasion to a depth of 6 mm on sectioning where the myometrium measures 18 mm. The lower uterine segment and cervix are unremarkable. The fallopian tubes and ovaries are unremarkable.

(1-4) Tumour, posterior wall, full thickness.
(5) Tumour, fundus.
(6) Anterior wall, full thickness.
(7) Lower uterine segment.
(8-9) Cervix, anterior and posterior.
(10) Right fallopian tube and ovary.
(11) Left fallopian tube and ovary.
(12-13) Right pelvic sentinel lymph nodes (2).
(14) Left pelvic sentinel lymph node (1).

Specimen and tumour
- Procedure: Total hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy; pelvic
  lymphadenectomy, para-aortic lymphadenectomy, omentectomy
- Hysterectomy type: Laparoscopic, robotic-assisted
- Specimen integrity: Intact
- Tumour site: Endometrium (posterior wall and fundus)
- Tumour size: 35 mm in greatest dimension (35 x 30 x 12 mm)

Microscopic findings
- Histologic type: Carcinosarcoma
- Histologic grade: High-grade (non-endometrioid carcinoma)
- Tumour histology:
  Sections show a carcinosarcoma. The tumour is biphasic, composed of a high-grade carcinomatous component with serous features and a heterologous sarcomatous component with rhabdomyoblastic differentiation (rhabdomyosarcoma), with an abrupt transition between the two components. Tumour necrosis is present. Myometrial invasion is by irregular infiltrative glands eliciting a stromal response.
- Mismatch repair (MMR) immunohistochemistry: Not performed
- p53 immunohistochemistry: Not performed
- POLE status: Not performed
- Molecular classification: Not performed
- Myometrial invasion: Estimated 50% or greater myometrial invasion
  - Depth of myometrial invasion: 14 mm
  - Myometrial thickness: 18 mm
  - Percentage of myometrial invasion: 78%
- Adenomyosis: Not identified
- Uterine serosa involvement: Not identified
- Lower uterine segment involvement: Not identified
- Cervical stromal involvement: Not identified
- Other tissue / organ involvement: Not identified
- Lymphovascular invasion: Not identified
- Perineural invasion: Not identified
- Peritoneal / ascitic fluid: Not submitted / unknown

Margins
- Ectocervical / vaginal cuff margin: Uninvolved by carcinoma
- Parametrial / paracervical margin: Not applicable

Lymph nodes
- Pelvic lymph nodes: 10 examined; 2 involved
  - Macrometastasis (more than 2 mm): 2
  - Largest metastatic deposit: 6 mm
  - Extranodal extension: Not identified
- Para-aortic lymph nodes: 6 examined; 1 involved
  - Macrometastasis (more than 2 mm): 1
  - Largest metastatic deposit: 9 mm
  - Extranodal extension: Present

Distant metastasis
- Distant metastasis: Omentum

Additional findings
- None

UTERUS WITH CERVIX AND BILATERAL ADNEXA, total hysterectomy and bilateral
salpingo-oophorectomy with pelvic lymphadenectomy, para-aortic lymphadenectomy
and omentectomy
- CARCINOSARCOMA, high grade, invading half or more of the myometrium
- no lymphovascular space invasion; cervix and adnexa uninvolved
- 2 of 10 pelvic lymph nodes involved; 1 of 6 para-aortic lymph nodes involved;
  metastatic carcinoma in the omentum

Carcinosarcoma is a biphasic tumour of metaplastic carcinoma and is staged and managed as a high-grade endometrial carcinoma; the carcinomatous and sarcomatous components, including any heterologous elements, are described above.

checks.message: Histologic grade derived: High-grade (non-endometrioid carcinoma) - carcinosarcoma is high grade by definition and is not FIGO graded.
MMR immunohistochemistry is not recorded; universal MMR testing is recommended for endometrial carcinoma.
FIGO 2023 (reference, not reported): IVB - abdominal peritoneal metastasis beyond the pelvis
